# enterprise-shift: the stewards work their tickets

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

One shift of the enterprise: the engine that takes open tickets from [`data/enterprise/tickets/`](../../../../../data/enterprise/tickets/README.md), works each through the [program workflow](../../../../../packages/improvement/program/README.md) in its own git worktree and session, has an independent reviewer decide on the result, assembles the approved changes onto the development branch, recertifies them there, and pushes them with the shift's ledger lines and record. [`driver.ts`](driver.ts) is the engine, [`shift.ts`](shift.ts) its pure half, and `pnpm run enterprise -- shift` ([`scripts/enterprise.ts`](../../../../../scripts/enterprise.ts)) the command that launches one shift on the operator's Claude Code route. The [Agent Note](../../../../../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-28-enterprise-shift-engine.md) records the decisions.

## What one shift does

1. **Clone.** `git clone --branch <branch> --single-branch` of the remote into `<scratch>/repo`, borrowing objects from the local repository when git can (`--reference-if-able`; a shallow local repository lends none, and the clone then fetches everything). The tip it was cut at is the base revision of every worktree; `remote.origin.pushurl` is set to an unreachable value, so a department that pushes through `origin` reaches nothing.
2. **Select.** The clone's queue is read and validated ([`scripts/enterprise-tickets.ts`](../../../../../scripts/enterprise-tickets.ts)); its `data/enterprise/ledger.jsonl` closes a ticket whose latest line was shipped or rejected by review; `--next <n>` takes the first `n` open tickets in queue order (fewest attempts, a halt on the usage limit not counting as one; then priority; then each division in turn; then id), `--tickets <id,...>` the named ones.
3. **Start.** Before any department runs, the shift appends its start line to `data/enterprise/shift-starts.jsonl` — `{ type: "shift-start", at, shift, tickets, base, host, pid, implementer }` — commits it with `--no-verify` and, with `--push`, pushes it fast-forward (a moved tip is fetched and the commit rebased onto it, the file merging by line union; a start that cannot be pushed in three rounds stops the shift with exit 2 before any department runs). Every worktree is cut from that commit. A start line whose shift has no ticket line in the ledger was cut off by a container reset: unless its host is this one and its pid is alive, each of its tickets still in the queue gets a ticket line under the dead shift's id with `department.outcome: "abandoned"` and a reason starting `abandoned: container reset`, written in the same commit and counted as an attempt before the shift selects.
4. **Program.** One program spec: one department per ticket (key `t-nnnn`, the ticket id lowered), the `implementing` preset, the ticket's budget as its caps, and a standard of the ticket's acceptance commands followed by the engine's checks — `engine-committed` (the branch carries a commit past the base), `engine-scope` (`git diff --name-only` with every scope prefix and every generated path of the queue policy excluded lists nothing), `engine-whitespace` (`git diff --check`) and, for a queue whose policy names a documentation gate (this repository's names `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing`), `engine-documentation`, which runs that gate whenever the diff touches a Markdown document and passes without it otherwise; the integration and the recertification run the same gate over the merged and the assembled change. The queue policy's generated paths — for this repository the outputs of the `gen-*` scripts `pnpm run doc-sync` checks, the subsystem pages carrying `type-equiv` pastes, and their Chinese sides and pair records — are inside every ticket's scope, because a change that makes one stale must regenerate it wherever it lives. The objective names the ticket, the seat from the roster, the task, the scope, the acceptance commands, how to bring a generated file back in line (run the generator `doc-sync` names, update a drifted `type-equiv` block on both sides, re-record the pairs), and points the department at `CLAUDE.md` and the package README. When `ENTERPRISE_HEAVY_LOCK` names a lock file, every acceptance command the policy marks heavy (one containing `pnpm run typecheck`, `--coverage` or `pnpm run doc-sync`) runs as `flock <lock> bash -c '<command>'` — in the department's standard, the integration and the recertification — so it waits for every other heavy run on the machine that takes the same lock, and the objective asks the department to run such commands itself the same way. The program runs every check under its `checkTimeoutMs`, which the composition sets to a department's whole wall budget. Every worktree is added and installed offline (`pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile`, when the repository has a lockfile) before the program starts, so the acceptance commands find an installed workspace. The program's own integration merges every certified department and repeats every ticket's acceptance over the merged head. The program is composed without a human release gate (`requireSignoff: false`): no person reviews an unattended shift, so nothing is signed in anyone's name, and the record states the spec freeze and the release as the engine's own decisions.
5. **Review.** Each certified department is reviewed in a session that never saw it: a fresh id with no parent and no seed, the `reviewing` preset (`role: judge`), every global tool restricted away (`tools.restrict({ allow: [] })`, because the deployment's tools are global rows and a reviewer with a shell could read the department's worktree), an empty working directory of its own under `<scratch>/review/`, and three messages — the standing instruction, the ticket with the queue's generated paths, which the instruction counts inside its scope, and the evidence (`git diff <base> <revision>`, the messages of the branch's commits, and every check's output, each bounded). The answer's first `verdict: approve|reject` line decides; an answer naming neither rejects.
6. **Assemble.** Approved departments are squashed onto the base in ticket order, one commit per ticket, authored and committed as `Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` (the clone's `user.name` and `user.email`, which the department commits share), whose message names the shift (`Shift: Daliesk shift <id>`), the ticket, the seat, the program id, both sessions, and ends with `Co-Authored-By: <the department's model>` and the `Claude-Session:` line. The engine's own commits pass `--no-verify`: the change was certified by the ticket's acceptance, and the clone's git hooks are the contributor's, installed for the departments by the offline install. When every department was approved, the assembled tree must equal the program's certified merged tree; every assembled ticket's acceptance then runs again over the assembled tree in the clone's own checkout. A squash that conflicts, a digest that differs, or an acceptance that fails ships nothing and records why.
7. **Ship.** The ledger lines and the record are committed after the assembled commits. With `--push`, the remote tip is fetched: when it moved, the assembled commits are rebased onto it, recertified there, and the ledger rewritten around their new hashes; a rebase that conflicts ships nothing and still pushes the ledger. The push is one fast-forward update of the branch, tried up to three rounds while the tip keeps moving, and passes `--no-verify` as the engine's commits do: it carries certified work and machine-written data, and the clone's pre-push hook typechecks a root that is not installed when nothing was assembled. A shift that ships nothing still pushes its ledger lines and record.
8. **Halt.** The first `turn/end` whose failure carries the LLM seam's `QUOTA` code — the route's usage-limit notice as [the seam classifies it](../../../../../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-27-route-limit-halts-the-run.md) — blocks that department's goal with `route-limit`, so its attempt ends without a validation run; every later department blocks on its first refused turn; nothing is reviewed, assembled, or shipped; every unfinished ticket's line reads `halted: limit (resets at <instant>)`; the driver exits 3.

## The ledger and the record

`data/enterprise/ledger.jsonl` gains one line per ticket per shift: `{ type: "ticket", at, shift, ticket, seat, division, programId, implementer, model, department: { outcome, sessionId }, checks: [{ id, ok }], review: { verdict, sessionId }, integration: { outcome }, shipped: { commit } | null, reason, tokens, seconds }`. `department.outcome` is `certified`, `failed`, `blocked`, `abandoned`, `pending` or `halted`; `review.verdict` is `approve`, `reject` or `none`; `integration.outcome` is `merged`, `skipped`, `conflict`, `checks-failed`, `digest-mismatch` or `not-shipped`. A ticket is closed once its latest line is shipped or rejected; any other line leaves it open for a later shift. The engine reads only ticket lines: a line without `type` counts as one, and a line of any other `type` — the enterprise functions' `function` lines share the file — is skipped.

`data/enterprise/shifts/<UTC date>-<shift id>/` holds `result.json` (the shift, the program report, the `decisions` — the spec freeze and the release, each naming the machine principal `daliesk-enterprise-shift` with `decidedBy: "the enterprise-shift engine, shift <id>"` over the SHA-256 of the selected tickets — every ticket's line with the reviewer's rationale, the halt), `manifest.json` (the base, the branch, the composition, every file's SHA-256) and `sessions/<session id>.jsonl` for every session of the shift — the program ledger, each department, each review, the integration. Credential-shaped strings are cut from every recorded byte and counted in `result.json`.

## The two compositions

[`cordis.yml`](cordis.yml) is the keyless half: every session runs on the `cli-mock` route of [`enterprise-llm.ts`](enterprise-llm.ts), whose departments are scripted per ticket of [`seed/`](seed/): `T-0001` delivers, `T-0002` delivers the wrong output, `T-0003` delivers and is rejected by the scripted reviewer, `T-0004` also writes outside its scope, `T-0005` moves the remote tip before it commits; `DSH_TEST_ENTERPRISE_LIMIT=1` makes every department turn fail with the `QUOTA` code and a stated reset. [`overlays/claude-code.cordis.yml`](overlays/claude-code.cordis.yml) is the real one: the scripted route disabled, the operator's Claude Code installation inserted, `DSH_ENTERPRISE_MODEL` (default `sonnet`) as every session's model, and the subagent seam composed so that `--implementer subagent` can delegate each department to Claude Code itself. Both carry the program's `checkTimeoutMs: 2700000` and the bash executor's `maxTimeoutMs: 2700000`, which the executor caps every timeout at; a department's own commands keep the executor's two-minute default.

## Running it keyless

```sh
pnpm exec vitest run --config vitest.e2e.config.ts examples/headless-agent/tests/enterprise-shift.e2e.ts
```

[`enterprise-shift.e2e.ts`](../../enterprise-shift.e2e.ts) seeds a bare remote from `seed/` and runs four shifts against it, each clone made from a git template whose `pre-push` hook refuses every push and each shift under a heavy lock of its own, which `seed/checks/coverage.sh`, the heavy acceptance command of `T-0001`, passes only while held: `T-0001,T-0002,T-0004` (one ticket ships, one fails its acceptance, one fails the scope check; the remote gains the ticket commit and the shift commit past the refusing hook), `T-0003` (certified, rejected, not shipped, closed in the ledger; two earlier start lines without an end are on the remote, and the one from another host closes its ticket as abandoned while the one whose process on this host is alive is left alone), `T-0005` (the tip moves, the shift rebases, recertifies and ships) and the limit halt over two tickets. [`enterprise-shift.spec.ts`](../../enterprise-shift.spec.ts) covers selection, the start lines and the abandoned lines they close, the compiled standard with its heavy lock and generated paths, the objective and the reviewer's ticket, the verdict line, the commit message and the redaction; [`scripts/enterprise.spec.ts`](../../../../../scripts/enterprise.spec.ts) the command line, the lock and the sweep.

## Running it for real

```sh
DSH_ENTERPRISE_SCRATCH=/path/outside/the/repository pnpm run enterprise -- shift --next 2 --push
```

The command needs the `claude` CLI installed and logged in, an installed workspace (the clone installs offline from the same store), and push access to `origin`. `ENTERPRISE_HEAVY_LOCK=<absolute path>` makes the heavy acceptance runs take that lock; the shift itself must never run under it, because its own checks could then never acquire it. `--tickets <id,...>` names tickets instead of `--next`, `--implementer subagent` delegates departments to Claude Code, `--model <id>` picks the product model, `--branch <name>` another branch than the development branch, `--keep` keeps the clone, and `--composition <path>` another composition. The wrapper writes `<scratch>/<shift id>/run.log` and the driver's session logs under `<scratch>/<shift id>/.sessions/`; a clone whose push failed is kept and named on stderr, every other clone is removed when the shift ends, and clones a day old are swept when the next shift starts.

The command is safe for an unattended schedule. `<scratch>/shift.lock` names the running shift's pid; a second shift refuses to start while that pid is alive (exit 4) and replaces the lock of a shift that died. Nothing reaches the remote before the one push at the end, so an interrupted shift leaves the branch as it found it and its next run selects from the ledger the branch carries. Exit codes: 0 for a shift that ran to its end (whether or not it shipped), 2 when the push failed in every round, 3 for a halt at the route limit, 4 for a shift refused by the lock.
